newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher with dollar bonds leading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher with dollar bonds leading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday led by dollar-linked bonds, with traders saying they expect yields on most bonds to continue falling.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 107.64
Volume including Makams was a moderate 138 million shekels.

"The market was up across the board today. There is a lot of money in the market. Provident funds and insurance companies have a lot of liquidity, which they are investing in the bond market," said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment.
"Players are investing in all kinds of bonds because there is still a lot of uncertainty about how the depreciation (of the shekel) will affect prices," he said.

Dollar-linked bonds led the rises, after the dollar gained against the shekel in early trading on Wednesday, Alt said. The trend reversed later in the day, and the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5690 shekels against 3.5730 on Tuesday.

After the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates on June 18, the shekel fell sharply against the dollar. After winning back some of its losses, the shekel has generally been trading lower in the last week.
The rise of the dollar against the shekel has prompted fears of a boost in inflation.

"Traders are afraid of inflation and so they are buying CPI-linked bonds. On the other hand, unlinked bonds have risen as well. Despite the depreciation of the shekel the coming CPIs are expected to be less than one percent a month," said Roy Meir of Simodan.
"All in all the market is positive with players foreseeing a continued fall in yields," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
